concepts.heading: Anatomy Beyond the Binary
concepts.plain: Most of us were taught too little about bodies, and some of it was shaming.

concepts.heading: Inclusive Language for Real Bodies
concepts.alt: A guide holding an open textbook and a speech bubble with a heart, speaking kindly
concepts.plain: Use words for body parts that fit the person, not their assumed gender.

concepts.heading: Pleasure-Relevant Anatomy
concepts.plain: School taught how babies are made. It skipped which parts feel good.

concepts.heading: Anatomical Diversity Is Normal
concepts.alt: Four guides standing together in a row with different heights and builds, arms around each other
concepts.plain: Bodies come in endless shapes, sizes and colours. Yours is normal.

concepts.heading: A Trauma-Informed Perspective
concepts.plain: If you feel shame or distance from your body, go gently. You set the pace.

checks.prompt: Why does the lesson pay attention to the words used for anatomy?
options: Only doctors may name body parts
checks.explanation: Language matters. Language matters in anatomy education. Many people use terms for their bodies that differ from clinical language, and both are valid.

checks.prompt: What does the lesson say about differences between bodies?
options: Bodies vary far more than textbooks suggest
checks.explanation: Bodies vary far more than textbooks suggest. Bodies vary far more than most anatomy textbooks suggest.

2f611ea6-a996-4b55-a0ec-6ca2372172df.takeaway: Bodies vary widely, and yours is normal.

concepts.heading: The Old Model of Arousal
concepts.alt: A guide drawing a straight line with four dots on a board
concepts.plain: The old idea was that arousal follows one straight line of steps.

concepts.heading: Non-Linear and Circular Models
concepts.alt: A guide drawing looping circles and waves on a board, smiling
concepts.plain: Real arousal loops, pauses and starts in different places.

concepts.heading: Arousal Non-Concordance
concepts.alt: A guide holding a thought bubble with a red cross while a small gauge beside her points to green
concepts.plain: Your body can react when your mind is not into it, and the other way round.

concepts.heading: Context, Safety, and Connection
concepts.plain: Feeling safe and connected makes arousal much easier.

concepts.heading: Orgasm Is Not the Goal
concepts.alt: A guide relaxing in a hammock with a crossed-out finish flag beside him
concepts.plain: Chasing orgasm makes it harder. Enjoying the moment works better.

concepts.heading: Inclusive Arousal
concepts.plain: Arousal looks different across bodies, ages, abilities and medicines.

checks.prompt: Your body shows physical arousal but your mind is not interested. What is this called?
checks.explanation: Arousal non-concordance. One of the most important concepts in modern sex science is arousal non-concordance — the phenomenon where your body's physical arousal response doesn't match your mental/emotional experience of desire.

checks.prompt: Watching and judging yourself during sex instead of feeling it is called…
checks.explanation: Spectatoring. When orgasm becomes the goal, it often becomes harder to achieve — a phenomenon sex therapists call "spectatoring."

ef0e57b8-01aa-4169-a14c-14e36ceea6f2.takeaway: Arousal does not follow one straight line, and your body reacting is not the same as wanting.

concepts.heading: The Body Image-Sexuality Connection
concepts.alt: A guide giving her reflection in a mirror a warm smile, a heart between them
concepts.plain: How you feel about your body affects how much you enjoy sex.

concepts.heading: How Shame Shows Up in Intimacy
concepts.alt: A guide hiding behind a big blanket, peeking over it with worried eyes
concepts.plain: Body shame shows up as hiding, avoiding, or watching yourself instead of feeling.

concepts.heading: Embodiment: Coming Home to Your Body
concepts.alt: Eyes closed with her hands on her belly, a soft glow around her whole body
concepts.plain: Embodiment means feeling your body from the inside, not judging it from outside.

concepts.heading: All Bodies Are Sexual Bodies
concepts.plain: Every body deserves pleasure and closeness. No body is left out.

checks.after: How Shame Shows Up in Intimacy
checks.prompt: Turning down intimacy so you will not be seen or touched is which shame pattern?
checks.explanation: Avoidance. Avoidance means declining intimacy to avoid being seen or touched.

checks.after: Embodiment: Coming Home to Your Body
checks.prompt: Feeling your body from the inside instead of judging how it looks is called…
checks.explanation: Embodiment. Embodiment is the practice of being fully present in your physical experience — feeling your body from the inside rather than evaluating it from the outside.

24232af6-d8d7-4cde-9a06-330312fe2eb7.takeaway: Feeling at home in your body makes pleasure easier. Every body deserves it.

concepts.heading: Sexual Wellness as Self-Care
concepts.alt: Wrapped in a cosy robe holding a cup of tea with heart-shaped steam
concepts.plain: Looking after your sexual self is ongoing self-care, like sleep or exercise.

concepts.heading: Integrating Embodiment Into Daily Life
concepts.plain: Small moments of noticing your body during the day add up.

concepts.heading: Pelvic Floor Awareness
concepts.alt: A guide doing a calm seated stretch on a yoga mat
concepts.plain: The pelvic floor is a set of muscles low in your hips. It can be too tight or too weak.

concepts.heading: The Foundations of Sexual Wellness
concepts.alt: A guide holding a pillow, an apple and a water bottle, a moon icon above
concepts.plain: Sleep, stress, movement and food all affect your sex life.

concepts.heading: When to Seek Professional Support
concepts.plain: Pain or distress that will not go away is a good reason to see a professional.

concepts.heading: Your Personal Wellness Toolkit
concepts.alt: A guide opening a toolbox filled with hearts, a feather and a candle
concepts.plain: Build your own mix of habits. There is no single right way.

options: Muscles that support the bladder, bowel and reproductive organs
checks.explanation: Muscles that support the bladder, bowel and reproductive organs. The pelvic floor is a group of muscles that supports your bladder, bowel, and reproductive organs.

checks.prompt: Which everyday factor does the lesson say suppresses desire hormones when you lack it?
checks.explanation: Sleep. Sleep deprivation suppresses hormones involved in desire.

ad816ede-61c6-4dd6-a1f4-54228ad68386.takeaway: Looking after your sexual self is everyday self-care, built from small habits.
